title: Form fields need a visible label, not only a title
summary: A field is named only by a title attribute. Add a visible label so everyone, including keyboard and touch users, can see what the field is for.
problem: A form field gets its name only from a title attribute, or from a hidden label or aria-describedby. The title shows as a tooltip only when a mouse pointer hovers over it, so most people never see what the field is for.
whoItAffects: Touch screen users and keyboard users never see a hover tooltip. People with memory or attention difficulties lose track of what a field is for when no text stays on screen. Screen readers may also handle titles inconsistently.
whyItMatters: This is a recommended practice rather than a WCAG failure. A visible label stays on screen while someone types, enlarges the click target and gives screen reader and voice users the same name that sighted users read.
steps: Find the field in the scan result and note its title attribute.
Add a visible <label> with a for attribute that matches the field's id, and use the title text as a starting point for the wording.
Remove the title attribute if it only repeats the label. Keep it only when it adds extra help.
If the design needs a compact form, keep the visible label small rather than hiding it.
before:
<form role="search" action="/search">
  <input type="search" name="q" title="Search products">
  <button type="submit">Go</button>
</form>
after:
<form role="search" action="/search">
  <label for="q">Search products</label>
  <input type="search" id="q" name="q">
  <button type="submit">Go</button>
</form>
howToCheck: Look at the page without moving the mouse over the field. If you cannot see text that names it, the field depends on a title or hidden label. A visible label should be on screen at all times.
